text: ← All problemsA subunit Rényi threshold for exponential-maximal iid entropy incrementsFor a probability density $f$ on $\mathbb R$ and $0<p<1$, define $h_p(f)=\frac{\log\int_{\mathbb R}f(x)^p\,dx}{1-p},\qquad (f*f)(s)=\int_{\mathbb R}f(t)f(s-t)\,dt,\qquad \Delta_p(f)=h_p(f*f)-h_p(f),$ whenever the two power integrals are finite and strictly positive. Thus $\Delta_p(f)$ is the Rényi entropy increment of the sum of two independent random variables with density $f$. Let $e(x)=e^{-x}\mathbf1_{[0,\infty)}(x)$. Subunit threshold question. Does there exist $p_0\in(0,1)$ such that for every $p_0<p<1$ and every log-concave probability density $f$ with the required finite positive moments, $\Delta_p(f)\le\Delta_p(e)?$ This is the one-dimensional necessary consequence of the proposed exponential-maximizer branch in the unnumbered paragraph after (1.2), p. 2, of Fu–Li. It is distinct from the numbered Shannon conjecture ($p=1$), and does not ask about the proposed cube-uniform branch below the threshold.ReferencesFu–Li, A reverse entropy power inequality for iid log-concave random variables, arXiv:2510.09206v3, p. 2, unnumbered paragraph after (1.2). https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.09206v300Posted by MJ KangPosted just nowEdit problemDelete problemProgress summaryRefreshNever refreshedNothing recorded yet.
